standing_rules: A skip is not a success; an empty state is not a clean one; measured zero must look different from never ran.
Never fail-soft a create call; preserve the error envelope.
'Set in the environment' and 'works' are different claims — run check:secrets before blaming code.
Run the SQL with the merge, never after.
An unpriced model id fails loud, never $0.
Trust source, git log, and the tracker over any prose claiming completeness; close items with file:line in the same commit.
Ledger what is unproven — today: the publish->lift loop, and each UI surface until its soak passes.
Closing a task is an act on a verifier's word, never the implementer's. The agent that wrote the code never closes it.
A change to the orchestration tooling is itself ledger work. The machine is not exempt from the discipline it enforces.
Trace a call site to an HTTP route or a cron entry before describing it as live. A correct file:line proves a line exists, not that anything reaches it.

Close an item only when, in the same commit, its box is ticked, the commit body cites the file:line where the change lives, and the acceptance criterion was exercised — run, not read and not reasoned about. If it could not be exercised here, the item is blocked with the reason, never closed.

tasks.title: Unique partial index on scan_jobs(brand) while running
tasks.detail: Closes the fail-open duplicate-scan TOCTOU: a DB error during hasActiveScanForBrand currently allows concurrent duplicate scans.
tasks.accept: Migration applies cleanly; a concurrent duplicate insert is rejected by the database, not by application logic.

notes.text: claimed

Migration 007 adds a unique partial index on lower(btrim(brand)) over the running statuses. The predicate cannot include heartbeat freshness (partial-index predicates must be IMMUTABLE), so createScanJob resolves the violation: a live holder is a typed DuplicateScanError -> 409, a crashed holder is failed and the insert retried once, so a brand is never locked forever. isDuplicateScanViolation is deliberately narrow — a connection error or a different constraint is NOT reported as 'already scanning'. A drift guard fails if db.js SCAN_JOB_RUNNING and the index predicate disagree. Exercised against a REAL PostgreSQL 16 cluster started locally, not just unit-tested.

ACCEPT MET and VERIFIED IN A BROWSER, not just in source. The route now branches on res.status === 404 for the genuine no-scans case and sets an error for every other non-ok status and for a thrown fetch. The shell takes an error prop and returns its own branch BEFORE the empty state — ordering matters, since a later branch would still fall through. ALL THREE STATES EXERCISED against the dev server: a brand with no scans renders 'Your dashboard is waiting' (404 -> empty, unchanged); a forced 503 renders 'We couldn't reach your data ... This is a problem on our side, not a missing report — your existing scans are unaffected' with a Try again button; and /dashboard/italica renders the real dashboard with 38 readings on record. Screenshot taken of the error state; it matches the design system. THE COPY IS PART OF THE FIX. The old behaviour told a user with a year of history that they had never scanned, and offered them a button to spend scan budget fixing an outage that was ours. The error state deliberately offers a retry and does NOT offer to run a scan, and a test asserts that — a future edit that drops a 'Run a visibility check' button into it fails. Four tests, source-level because this repo has no component-render harness; they pin the two load-bearing decisions and the branch ordering. TEETH: collapsing the 404 and error paths back together fails 1 of 4. Suite green.

rejected: REJECTED. A verifier reproduced a REAL DB outage over HTTP and the dashboard still lands in the first-run state. ROOT CAUSE: getScansForBrand FAILS QUIET at src/lib/db.js:179-196 — returns [] on error and [] when supabase is null, NEVER throws. postgrest-js turns network/DNS/5xx failures into {data:null,error} rather than rejecting (client built with no throwOnError), so the routes 500-on-throw guard at src/app/api/scans/[brand]/latest/route.js:26-34 is DEAD CODE for this failure mode — the routes own comment admits it. Italica has 38 real scans; with the DB down the user is told they never scanned and offered the Run a visibility check button — verbatim the bug this task exists to kill. The only 503 in the API is /api/health:60, which the dashboard never calls, so the forced-503 browser check exercised a status the real system cannot emit for a DB outage. Records what it applied: schema_migrations (filename, checksum, applied_at) is created first and written inside each file's transaction; the live table now holds all nine rows with checksums. Transaction per file: BEGIN / apply / record / COMMIT with ROLLBACK on failure, so a migration that dies halfway no longer leaves a schema no file describes for the next run to layer over. Reports a DB missing 006 as incomplete: the verify list stopped at 005 and now covers 001-009 keyed BY MIGRATION FILE, checked against the catalog, printing INCOMPLETE and setting exit 1 on any miss. Verified live: all 24 expected objects across 9 migrations tick, exit 0. THIS IS THE TOOL THAT FAILED TODAY, so two details are deliberate. The old runner printed 'Migrations applied successfully.' BEFORE verifying — the sentence that made a broken run look fine; success is now claimed only after the check, and a test asserts that string cannot return. And function existence is checked via pg_proc, not to_regclass, because 009 was found this morning with its TABLE present and its increment_scan_rate_limit FUNCTION absent — a to_regclass-only check would have passed on exactly that state. Also added: a checksum mismatch warns that a migration was edited after being applied, so the file no longer describes the database. GUARD IS AGAINST STALENESS, not against today's list: it walks supabase/migrations and fails if any file lacks an entry, and also fails on an entry for a file that no longer exists. TEETH: deleting the 006 entry — the literal C10 shape — fails 2 of 6.

rejected: REJECTED on evidence integrity and on the regression guard. THE IMPLEMENTATION IS GENUINELY GOOD AND ALL THREE ACCEPT CLAUSES HOLD BEHAVIOURALLY — the verifier proved that themselves. DO NOT REWRITE scripts/setup-supabase.mjs's logic.

WHAT IS VERIFIED. The original failure was reproduced: the old runner against a DB missing 006-009's objects printed "Migrations applied successfully." plus 17 ticks and exit 0; the new runner on the identical stub state prints 6 crosses, INCOMPLETE and exit 1. Clause 2 was proven properly, with a stub pg client and a full query log: BEGIN, migration body, INSERT INTO schema_migrations, COMMIT are ALL TAGGED THE SAME TRANSACTION ID, so the recording is genuinely inside the apply's transaction rather than adjacent to it; and a mid-file failure gives BEGIN, throw, ROLLBACK in the same transaction with no INSERT, no COMMIT, exit 1, and later migrations not attempted. Clause 3 exercised against a stubbed catalog omitting 006's sentinel: INCOMPLETE, exit 1. The verifier also reproduced the exact 2026-08-30 state — 009's table present, its function absent — giving a tick for the table and a cross for the function. THE pg_proc CATCH IS REAL AND CONFIRMED ON LIVE PROD: to_regclass returns NULL for increment_scan_rate_limit while pg_proc finds it, so a to_regclass-only check literally cannot see that function. Good catch, correctly implemented. THE GUARD WALKS: dropping a new migration file in makes it fail NAMING the file, and deleting the 006 entry from EXPECTED_OBJECTS fails 2 of 6 as claimed. schema_migrations holds 9 rows with real checksums that match the implementer's checkout byte for byte.

WHY IT FAILS.

(1) TWO OF THREE EVIDENCE CITATIONS POINT AT UNCHANGED, UNRELATED LINES. setup-supabase.mjs:16 is "import pg from 'pg';" — pre-existing, untouched by the commit; the added import is createHash on line 15. setup-supabase.mjs:112 is "if (process.env.SUPABASE_DB_HOST) {" — pre-existing connection-string plumbing, unrelated to the ledger, the transaction or the verify list. Only :40 lands inside the change, and it is a prose comment rather than the mechanism. Standing rule 6 exists so a citation proves where the change lives.

(2) THE REGRESSION GUARD CANNOT DETECT THE FAILURE IT EXISTS TO PREVENT. All six tests in src/lib/migrationsLedger.test.mjs are REGEXES OVER THE RUNNER'S SOURCE TEXT; nothing ever executes it. The verifier changed the failure branch to exitCode 0 and parked a dead "if (false) process.exitCode = 1;" in the success branch. The runner then PRINTED INCOMPLETE AND EXITED 0 ON A DB MISSING 006 — the literal C10 false success — and PASSED 6 OF 6 GUARDS. A syntactically broken runner that fails node --check also passes 6 of 6. assert.match(src, /INCOMPLETE/) checks the spelling of the criterion, not the criterion. This is the tool that failed on the day it was written; its own reliability is the thing under test.

(3) THE PREMATURE-SUCCESS ORDERING IS NOT PINNED. The test bans one literal string. Restoring "Migrations applied successfully" correctly fails 1 test, so that half of the note is true. But putting a DIFFERENT success sentence in the same pre-verification slot passes 6 of 6. Separately, setup-supabase.mjs:179 still prints "Migrations applied." before verification, so "success is claimed only after the check" is softer than stated — though the INCOMPLETE text does explicitly disclaim it, which is a deliberate mitigation.

(4) THE CHECKSUM LEDGER IS LINE-ENDING SENSITIVE AND SELF-ERASING. 001 and 006 are CRLF in the main tree and LF in any fresh, Linux or CI checkout, so running setup:db from an LF checkout warns that files nobody edited have CHANGED — and then the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET checksum at :165-170 OVERWRITES the recorded checksum. The drift signal fires exactly once and destroys its own evidence; the next run is silent. The column records what the last checkout looked like, not what was applied. This compounds R6.4.7, the mixed-line-endings task.

TO FIX: (a) repoint the three evidence lines at the ledger DDL, the transaction block and the INCOMPLETE branch. (b) Add a BEHAVIOURAL test that imports the runner with a stubbed pg — module.registerHooks mapping the "pg" specifier to a virtual module exporting a fake Client works cleanly on Node 26 and takes about 90 lines — asserting exitCode 1 when the catalog omits 006, that the ledger INSERT falls between BEGIN and COMMIT, and that a throwing body produces ROLLBACK with no INSERT. (c) Either assert the ordering positionally (indexOf of any success sentence greater than indexOf of the verify loop) or drop the ordering claim from the note. (d) Normalise line endings before hashing, or hash the parsed statements, and decide whether an upsert that erases drift is the behaviour you want.

TWO SMALLER OBSERVATIONS, not the basis of the verdict: the plan specified skipping versions already in schema_migrations, but the implementation re-applies every file every run — defensible given IF NOT EXISTS idempotency, but it makes applied_at mean "last re-applied", and all nine live rows carry the same timestamp. And the verify list probes one sentinel object for 006 while the file creates four more objects and three columns; sound as a proxy going forward because each file is now atomic, and the verifier confirmed read-only that 006 is in fact fully applied in prod, so nothing is currently masked.

The verifier wrote NOTHING to production: every query was a read on a read-only session, and the 006 row was left untouched — the C10 teeth were proven against the test's own fixture instead. 977/977 before and after.

Six files — brightdata, perplexity, chatgpt, firecrawl, gateway-catalog, and the pre-existing mimo. All carry status headers and pass the docStatus guard. Bright Data: the wrapped body (payload arrives as a JSON string under ), ai_overview in five shapes with texts winning, references under three different keys, and four failure modes with their retry semantics — including that a truncated body costs a 9s backoff, which is why a mock with an empty body wastes it before asserting anything. Firecrawl: optional means optional; UNCONFIGURED is not FAIL. GATEWAY-CATALOG is the one the task singled out and it is written as a rule with its two incidents, because it has now cost this project twice: the same misreading recurred on 2026-08-30 and survived a week in the roadmap, the handoff and my own first pass.
